Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Insurance Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Insurance Group's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer; David Wong, Chief Investment Officer; Emily Rivera, Chief Operating Officer; and Robert Hayes, Chief Claims Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Apex Insurance Group's performance for Q3 2024. We delivered strong results, driven by favorable customer acquisition cost trends, refinements in our actuarial assumptions, a fortified capital position with elevated statutory surplus, robust new business production volumes, manageable catastrophe losses relative to gross written premiums, and clear guidance on premium growth and combined ratio improvements. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation initiatives.

Michael, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Chen: Thank you, John. Good morning, everyone. As John mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $450 million, or $1.12 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included optimized customer acquisition costs, updates to actuarial assumptions, strong capital and surplus growth, surging new business volumes, controlled catastrophe impacts, and forward guidance on premiums and profitability metrics. Our combined ratio was 94.2%. Investment income for the quarter was $320 million. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with 450% RBC. Our expense ratio also improved to 29.5%.

Let me dive deeper into these elements, starting with customer acquisition cost trends, which continue to shine in our property & casualty and group life segments despite a competitive landscape. Customer acquisition cost, or CAC, remains a vital KPI for us, computed as total sales and marketing expenses—including digital ads, agent commissions, broker fees, and lead generation—divided by new annualized premium in force from newly acquired policies. We're intensely focused on refining this to sustain our leading lifetime value-to-CAC ratio of 4.2x, surpassing the peer average of 3.5x as per AM Best data.

The top line for Q3: blended CAC hit $287 per new policy, down 12% year-over-year from $326 in Q3 2022 and 4% sequentially from Q2's $299. This extends our streak of six consecutive quarters of CAC reduction, powered by a 22% increase in digital self-service conversions and gains from our AI-driven underwriting engine. This outperforms Progressive's $310 blended CAC last quarter and far exceeds Geico's $340-plus in direct auto, where heavy TV and search spending persists.

By channel, direct-to-consumer digital—now 58% of new business, up from 45% last year—showed the biggest drop, with CAC falling 18% year-over-year to $185. This stems from our updated mobile app incorporating telematics from partners like Cambridge Mobile Telematics, akin to Root Insurance but applied to our 15 million auto policyholders. Opt-ins for "DriveSafe Rewards" deliver 25% faster quotes, lifting conversions to 42% from 32% a year ago. Agent and broker channels, 35% of acquisitions, experienced a 7% CAC decline to $412, achieved by adjusting commissions through persistency-linked tiers—our 12-month persistency now at 87%, beating the NAIC industry average of 82%.

On products, personal lines dominated: auto CAC fell 15% to $210, aided by embedded insurance ties with fintechs like Affirm and auto dealers through our white-label API, echoing Allstate's dealer integrations. Homeowners' CAC was stable at $345, down 9% year-over-year, due to climate-risk modeling via ClimateAi partnership, enabling 10% lower premiums in risky areas like Florida after Hurricane Ian. Group life and health CAC edged up 5% to $620 from longer B2B cycles in uncertain economics, countered by 65% upsell rates on voluntary benefits like "FlexLife" critical illness riders.

Regionally, U.S.—72% of new premiums—saw CAC at $265, down 14% year-over-year, boosted by 30% better Google and Meta ad ROAS at 5.8x despite 8% higher CPMs from competition. Europe, 18% of acquisitions, dropped 9% to €310 ($335 equivalent), helped by GDPR-friendly personalization through SAP Emarsys CDP, though UK Brexit broker issues kept auto CAC at £280. Asia-Pacific, 10% of new business and fastest-growing, compressed 16% to A$420 ($280 USD), via WeChat mini-app quoting in China (35% conversion jump) and Singtel telco bundles in Southeast Asia, similar to AXA's approach. In emerging spots like India, CAC is ₹18,000 ($220), scaling through Jio ties.

These trends align with our "Acquire Smart, Retain Forever" approach. Year-to-date $45 million in tech spend includes GenAI chatbot "InsureBot" handling 70% of quotes at 92% accuracy, cutting call center costs 25%. Blockchain broker verification pilots target another 10% CAC cut in H1 2025. With industry combined ratios at 95.2% per PCI, we're favoring high-LTV bundles like home-auto (LTV $4,200) over low-margin renters. Blended payback is now 8 months from 11, fueling 12-15% premium growth in 2025 without margins eroding.

This CAC strength outshines peers like Travelers or Chubb facing 5-8% agent comp inflation. Full-year CAC guidance is $290, 11% below plan.

Next, changes in actuarial assumptions significantly shaped our results. Actuarial assumptions underpin our reserving and pricing across life & annuity, P&C, and group health, embedding margins for adverse deviation per NAIC and Solvency II.

This quarter's annual study used stochastic modeling, ML analytics, and SOA/Milliman data, responding to medical inflation, post-COVID longevity gains, climate-driven cat frequency, and Fed rate hikes' discount effects.

In life & annuity—45% of $250 billion liabilities—we extended longevity 1.5% for ages 65+, per SOA tables and our claims data, reflecting better cardio/cancer outcomes offset by 0.8% excess working-age mortality from long COVID. Impact: $285 million pre-tax reserve charge, 12 points to combined ratio, partly offset by $110 million from lower lapse assumptions (2.2% vs. 2.5% prior, due to FIA stickiness). Net: $175 million hit, or $0.42 EPS; EV down 3% but risk-adjusted margin at 18%, topping Athene. Europe Solvency II saw milder 0.9% shift, €45 million to SCR.

Discount rates rose 60 bps for P&C and 40 bps for life on 4.2% 10-year Treasury average; yields up to 4.8% from 4.5% on 65/35 allocation. Impact: $420 million releases, lifting P&C loss ratio 180 bps to 92.4%, driving 15% operating income growth to $1.2 billion. Offset by $95 million GLB variance from sticky behavior amid 22% S&P gains.

Morbidity trends: group health to 5.8% for 2025 from 5.4% on GLP-1 drugs and shortages; P&C workers' comp up 4.2% on AWAKEN inflation, auto severity 6.1%. Lapses down 0.7 points to 8.5% in commercial via LexisNexis telematics; expenses trimmed 2% by AI claims. Net $210 million charge; group health loss ratio 105.2% but improved 90 bps via Optum ties.

Overall: net $75 million unfavorable ($0.11 EPS), 4% of $2.76 adjusted EPS, offset by 11% premium growth and light cats. Accident year development +2.1 points, beating Travelers/Chubb.

Our $50 million Actuarial Modernization uses GenAI for 10,000 Monte Carlo runs and blockchain with Swiss Re, cutting cycles 40%, back-testing to 95%.

U.S. (75%): inflation/litigation drove P&C; VM-21 stable life. Europe/UK (15%): PRA matching cushioned; telematics lapses. APAC (10%): Japan 2.1% longevity; China health unwind.

Prudent reserving targets 14-16% risk-adjusted ROE, 7-10% MAD. Q4 neutral; $3 billion reinsurance cedes 25% Florida. Pricing to 105%+ adequacy.

Turning to capital position and statutory surplus, which fortify our strength. Consolidated statutory surplus: $15.2 billion at September 30, up 12.4% from $13.5 billion Q3 2023, outpacing Travelers (8%) and Chubb (10%). RBC at 452%, up 32 points from 420%, top-quartile A-rated per AM Best, above 400% target. Total qualified capital $18.4 billion, 1.8x leverage vs. 2.5x industry.

Drivers: $1.8 billion YTD earnings retention; $650 million Q3 underwriting income at 92.6% combined (beat 94-96% guide); $520 million prior-year development in workers' comp/auto via Optum/Cigna deals. Investments added $920 million on 4.2% yield (from 3.1%), 65/35 split, high-yield down to 5%. Cats $420 million (Helene/wildfires), net 15% retention via $2.5 billion excess covers from Lloyd's/Swiss Re, saving $1.2 billion.

Tech: internal model unlocked $450 million RBC via covariance for multi-peril/cyber; DFCC allocates dynamically; BlackLine/Moody's Axis speed modeling 40%.

Regions: U.S. Northeast/Midwest (55%) +15% on 9.2% packages/E&S; California (12%) +7% post-wildfires, telematics cut PML 18%; London Syndicate +20% D&O/cyber; Florida capped at $150 million/storm via Citizens cat bonds, cat load to 22% from 25%.

Forward: $1.2 billion buybacks ($400 million done at $145/share, 4-5% EPS accretion); 35% dividend, $1.05 pending; M&A like $500 million D&O tuck-in; cyber to $850 million (+28%), 18% ROC. Stress-tested for 200 bps cut ($600 million NAIC hit), $2.1 billion liquidity covers.

On new business production volume, we track annualized premium equivalent (APE) and policy counts. Q3 APE: $2.85 billion, +18% YoY from $2.42 billion, beating guide by 5%; 1.27 million policies, +12% from 1.13 million. Strongest since Q4 2021; TTM $11.2 billion, FY 15-17% growth.

P&C: $1.68 billion APE (+25%), 892,000 policies (+16%); commercial $1.1 billion on SBOPs; personal $580 million on AI-telematics auto (15% UBI share). Life/Health: $875 million (+9%), 285,000 (+5%); UL +14%, group +11%. Annuities: $295 million (+12%), 93,000 (+9%); FIAs $210 million via BlackRock.

Regions: North America $1.92 billion (+21%), 845K; Europe $0.52 billion (+11%), 210K on UL/UK motor; APAC $0.41 billion (+14%), 215K on bancassurance/micro-health.

ApexNow AI platform cut quote-to-bind 40%; IoT telematics 220 bps loss improvement; blockchain e-apps 85% STP. Prioritizing quality: CSM $1.4 billion, value/policy $2,240 (+6%), cross-sell 32%. Q4 APE $2.9-3.1 billion; FY policies 5.0-5.2 million.

Catastrophe losses totaled $1.42 billion, 2.4% of GWP, vs. $950 million/1.9% Q3 2022. YTD $3.8 billion/2.1%, on 2.0-2.5% guide. Ex-Idalia/Maui: 1.6%. North America 62% ($880 million, Idalia $650 million, 75% adjusted fast via Guidewire/EagleView); California $150 million. Europe 22% ($310 million, floods); APAC 12% ($170 million, Typhoon Doksuri, derisked 30% parametric).

Trends: +25% YoY inflation-adjusted, frequency +15% per RMS (hurricanes 1-in-30). Initiatives: $150 million cat modeling (AIR/ML on NOAA/ECMWF, PML +18%); $12 billion reinsurance (40% sidecars, -10% cost); 12% trim Florida/Texas, Cat Shield parametric $50 million; +15% rates.

Q4 $1.0-1.4 billion (2.2-2.4% FY); cat load 20% below peers.

Premium growth: Q3 net written +10.2% to $4.8 billion (beat 8-10%); book-to-bill 1.15x, retention 88.5%. P&C +11.5%, personal +7.8%, specialty +9.4%. U.S. +11.8%, int'l +6.9%.

FY2024 raised to 9-11% (Q4 10-12%, Q3 8-10% or $4.9-5.0 billion); 4-6% pricing, 2-3% volume. Enablers: ZenithEdge AI (+15% conversions), Guidewire cloud ($50 million savings); 5-7% rates; M&A $1.2 billion synergies. Risks: cats/inflation.

Combined ratio guidance: Q3 ex-cat 88.5%, full 102.3% (cats 12 points). FY2024 93-96% (Q4 91-94%, cats 4-6 points). Loss 63-65% (ex-cat 61%), expense 29-30%. 2025: 91-94%; 6-8% rates >5.2% trends; EagleEye AI 3.5 points savings; portfolio shifts, reinsurance -5%.

This positions us for 8-10% 2025 premiums, $1.2 billion underwriting income.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial P&C lines. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including AI-enhanced generalized linear models and telematics integrations for dynamic pricing.

David Wong: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in investment-grade corporates and fixed indexed annuities, yielding 4.8% amid stable rates.

Robert Hayes: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction, including Guidewire ClaimCenter and AI triage. We are seeing positive results in terms of reduced claims processing times, with 75% of cat claims adjusted in 30 days.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Alex Johnson with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Alex Johnson: Good morning. Can you provide more color on customer acquisition cost trends?

John Reynolds: Good morning, Alex. As Michael detailed, our CAC compression to $287 reflects digital efficiencies and channel optimizations, positioning us ahead of peers with a 4.2x LTV-CAC and payback under 9 months. This fuels sustainable growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of elevated catastrophe activity on your business?

Michael Chen: Good morning, Maria. Cats at 2.4% of GWP were managed via our robust reinsurance and modeling, keeping net impact contained and below peers. Our initiatives like parametrics and portfolio trims ensure resilience while supporting combined ratio goals.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Kim: What is the expected impact of potential regulatory changes in high-risk states like California and Florida on your underwriting strategy?

Lisa Patel: Good morning, David. We're proactively addressing scrutiny through rate filings backed by GLMs and cat models, alongside non-renewals in exposed areas. This maintains adequacy above 105% while expanding in lower-risk segments.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Patel: Thanks. On actuarial assumptions, how do you see the net impact evolving into 2025?

Michael Chen: Sarah, Q4 should be neutral, with discount tailwinds offsetting morbidity trends. Our modernization program ensures precision, supporting 14-16% ROE.

Operator: [No further questions at this time.]

John Reynolds: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
